title: User profile errors
executive_summary: user-service errors began at 21:03Z, about 2 minutes after a kernel nf_conntrack "table full" event on usr-node-3 (21:02Z). Error rate rose from ~0.4% to ~30% and timeouts from 0.05% to ~9%. Errors are PSQLException "connection refused" and "connection reset by peer" to postgres-primary:5432, so the failure is at the network/connection layer, not pool exhaustion (user-service DB connection utilisation stayed flat at ~30%, baseline 29.9%). The most likely cause is conntrack exhaustion on usr-node-3 dropping DB packets. This is unconfirmed: the log does not say whether other nodes are affected, and PostgreSQL-side telemetry is missing for the window.

hypotheses.description: nf_conntrack table exhaustion on usr-node-3 drops user-service -> postgres-primary connections, producing refused/reset errors and timeouts. Mechanism: The conntrack table filled on usr-node-3 at 21:02Z and the kernel began dropping packets. New and existing TCP sessions to postgres-primary:5432 from that node were refused or reset. user-service retries fail, which surfaces as DB errors and timeouts. Onset of the error spike (21:03Z) follows the kernel event by about one minute.

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): infrastructure_degradation in user-service - nf_conntrack table exhaustion on usr-node-3 drops user-service -> postgres-primary connections, producing refused/reset errors and timeouts.
corrective_actions: Drain or reschedule user-service pods off usr-node-3 and confirm the error rate returns to baseline
Raise nf_conntrack_max on usr nodes, or clear stale entries, then verify the table no longer fills
preventive_actions: Alert on nf_conntrack usage above 80% on all nodes
Review connection churn from user-service to postgres (pooling, keepalive) to reduce conntrack load
Optimise or schedule report_rollup() so it does not run during peak traffic
monitoring_recommendations: Track user-service error and timeout rate per node
Track conntrack count vs max per node
Restore postgres metrics-agent export so DB-side telemetry is complete

conclusion: The most probable cause is nf_conntrack table exhaustion on usr-node-3, which began at 21:02Z and dropped user-service's connections to postgres-primary, causing refused and reset errors from 21:03Z. There is no deployment or configuration change in the window. The status is PROBABLE rather than confirmed because per-node attribution and PostgreSQL-side telemetry are missing. The report_rollup slowness is a real but pre-existing issue that does not explain the step change at 21:03Z.
